scope: Static fixed-worked-example and supplied-formula checks; no driving claim or preset promotion.
limitations: Twenty-four fresh synthetic geometries in twelve mirrored pairs and repeated conditions are not independent driving trials.
The fixed six-example package adds intermediate arithmetic, target labels, repeated rules and question length together. A gain cannot identify a single internal mechanism or prove exact arithmetic.

The same full observation, raw named coordinates and five wheel choices are submitted for both prompts. Only candidate question text includes the fixed teaching examples; current-query calculations and targets are never supplied.
All worked-example numeric pairs are excluded from the test bank. Numerical disjointness does not establish generalization beyond this narrow synthetic geometry and supplied policy.
Coarse wheel answers cannot prove exact trigonometric execution. A supplied policy label is not an optimal driving action and static accuracy cannot qualify driving.
Heading-sign mismatch groups can differ in target magnitude; subgroup scores do not isolate a sign-conflict effect.
Endpoint errors count as incorrect in attempted accuracy; planned coverage and unrun cases remain separate.
recommendation: Retain damped as the live baseline and original application default. Six fixed worked examples improve this static score by6.25pp but fail overall,per-magnitude and gain gates; no native-menu continuation or live promotion.

interpretation: The examples package yields 34/48 correct versus 31/48 for its fresh literal control, a net gain of 3/48 (6.25 percentage points). This fails the declared ten-point gain and 90% overall thresholds. Full accuracy of 5/16 and straight accuracy of 13/16 also fail 85% per magnitude; moderate remains 16/16. No native validation is triggered.

Five individual pairs improve and two regress. Improvements comprise three full-right answers (05-b twice and 02-b once) and two straight answers (09-a once and 09-b once); both regressions are the same straight fixture, 03-b, across its two repetitions. Straight accuracy therefore stays 13/16 despite changed cases; all net gain is full-right.

Full-left remains 0/8 in both prompts. Full-right improves from 2/8 to 5/8. Every selected full wheel is RIGHT: the control chooses two and examples choose five. Balanced fixed demonstrations contain both left and right full answers, but the observed gain is one-sided and does not establish general magnitude calculation.

Control choices are 13 straight, 33 moderate and two full; example choices are 13 straight, 30 moderate and five full. All 35 nonzero choices in each prompt agree with raw-y sign. Correct sign does not establish magnitude, arithmetic or optimal control.

The four x=15-discriminating geometries give eight answers per prompt, with 4/8 correct in each. Full-target pair 08-a/b remains wrong with the moderate x=15 shortcut label; moderate-target pair 10-a/b remains correct, rejecting its full x=15 shortcut label. This mixed pattern does not identify a universal x-substitution or exact-arithmetic mechanism.

Across 24 cases, two-repeat scores improve on four cases, worsen on one and tie on 19. Both repeats correct rises from 15 to 16 cases; repeated exact choices match on 23/24 control cases and 22/24 example cases. These cases include mirrored pairs and repeated responses; descriptive counts are not independent reliability estimates.

Only the fixed demonstration package changes; its intermediate arithmetic, explicit answer labels, rule repetition and extra context length move together. The comparison does not identify which teaching feature or internal computation caused answer changes. These static supplied-policy scores do not qualify a live driver.
